title: Quantum coherence and Leggett-Garg inequality
authors: A. Jalal, S. M. Fazeli, M. M. Ettefaghi
abstract: In this paper, we attempt to establish the relationship between quantum coherence and the violation of the Leggett-Garg inequality. In particular, employing the Lindblad equation, we obtain the pseudo-density matrix for a damping system to study the effect of environment interaction on the violation of this inequality in a two-state quantum system. It is shown that the violation of the Leggett-Garg inequality can be observed as long as temporal evolution does not induce decoherence. This statement is independent of the initial state of the system. Furthermore, similar to the Horodecki criterion for the CHSH inequality (R. Horodecki et al. Phys. Lett. {\bf A200}, 340), we study necessary and sufficient conditions for violating the Leggett-Garg inequality. Hereby, under the circumstance that the inequality violation occurs, an upper bound for the time interval between consecutive measurements with respect to the time scale of interaction with the environment (the relaxation time) is obtained.
summary: This paper investigates how environmental decoherence affects the violation of the Leggett-Garg inequality (LGI) in open quantum systems. Using the Lindblad equation and pseudo-density matrices, the authors derive a quantitative criterion showing that LGI violation is suppressed over time by environmental noise. This establishes a direct measure linking coherence preservation to the feasibility of observing non-classical correlations.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a quantitative relationship between quantum coherence and the violation of the Leggett-Garg inequality (LGI) in open quantum systems.
main_result: It is shown that LGI violation persists only as long as environmental decoherence does not occur, leading to an upper bound on the measurement time interval relative to the environment's relaxation time scale.
method: The study employs the Lindblad master equation and utilizes the pseudo-density matrix (PDM) formalism to calculate temporal correlations across sequential measurements.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a two-state quantum system interacting with an environment, whose dynamics are governed by the Lindblad master equation. The analysis extends from isolated systems to open quantum systems.
key_observables: Violation of the Leggett-Garg inequality (LGI), quantum coherence, and the time-dependent correlation function $K_n$ or $M_R$.
important_parameters: The environmental relaxation time scale ($	au$) and damping rates ($\gamma_i$).
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include modeling open evolution via the Lindblad equation and assuming an idealized non-invasive measurement process.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how LGI violation ($K_4$ or $M_R$) decreases or vanishes as the time interval ($	au$) between measurements increases in the presence of environmental coupling.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework using the Lindblad equation for open systems. It then develops criteria (like PDM and derived bounds) to test LGI violation, contrasting results from isolated versus decohering environments to quantify coherence loss.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, quantitative link between fundamental non-classical resources (coherence) and macroscopic constraints (LGI), which is crucial for understanding the limits of quantum measurements in realistic noisy environments relevant to AMO physics.
